name: RHI Magnesita N.V.
executive_summary:
RHI Magnesita is the global leader in refractory products and systems for steel (~69–71% of revenue) and industrial high-temperature processes, listed on the FTSE 250 with a secondary Vienna listing. The quantitative screen flags a Strong Buy on cheapness (P/E 20.2, P/B 1.7), a 5.0% dividend yield, positive FCF yield, and GARP/risk-model passes — yet conviction on the screen is low (38%) and timing is neutral (RSI ~60).

The investment case rests on a cyclically depressed earnings base that management is lifting through self-help (pricing, plant network optimisation, SG&A cuts, Resco integration), strong cash conversion (>100% in 2024–25), and operational gearing to any steel/industrial recovery. FY2025 adjusted EBITA was €373m on revenue of €3,366m; H1 2026 adjusted EBITA rose 42% constant-currency to €165m despite flat CC revenue, confirming turnaround momentum.

The central debate is whether valuation adequately compensates for elevated leverage (2.9x net debt/pro forma adjusted EBITDA post-Resco), persistent Chinese export competition, deferred high-margin industrial projects (especially Glass), and FX headwinds — or whether self-help and deleveraging to ~2.6x by end-2026 unlock re-rating without a full cycle upturn.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, RHIM offers a globally dominant franchise trading below typical industrial multiples while paying a well-covered dividend (€1.80/share in 2025; 2.3x cover on adjusted EPS of €4.18). The screen passes four factor families — cheapness, dividend, GARP, and risk — with full data quality (20/20 metrics). Reported FCF was €214m in 2025 (Yahoo: €268m on a slightly different basis); adjusted operating cash flow was €391m with 105% cash conversion.

Business quality is better than the headline earnings decline suggests. Adjusted EBITA fell only 8% in 2025 despite a weak H1 (€141m at 8.4% margin) because H2 recovered sharply to €232m (13.7% margin) on pricing discipline, €70m of H2 cost savings, and Resco contribution (€184m revenue, €25m adjusted EBITA). H1 2026 extended this trajectory: adjusted EBITA +17% reported (+42% CC) to €165m at 10.3% margin, with steel margins expanding and FY2026 guidance held at €400m adjusted EBITA.

The 4PRO performance-based model, vertical integration (~42% raw material self-sufficiency), recycling leadership (15.9% global rate; 19.5% H1 2026), and M&A consolidation track record (Resco €391m, closed January 2025) support durable competitive positioning. ROIC was 9.5% in 2025 (down from 10.4% in 2024) but H1 2026 annualised ROIC improved to 8.4% from 5.8% in H1 2025.

The screen’s Strong Buy signal aligns with a name where reported IFRS earnings (EPS €1.82 in 2025) understate economic earnings (adjusted EPS €4.18) due to restructuring, ERP/digital spend, and amortisation — creating a classic value-in-transformation setup, albeit with cyclical and balance-sheet caveats the screen cannot fully capture.
financial_review:
*Primary source: RNS filing bodies unless noted.*

**Annual results**

| Metric | FY2024 (27 Feb 2025 RNS) | FY2025 (2 Mar 2026 RNS) | Change |
|--------|--------------------------|-------------------------|--------|
| Revenue | €3,487m | €3,366m | −3% reported; −1% CC |
| Adjusted EBITA | €407m (11.7%) | €373m (11.1%) | −8% |
| Adjusted EPS | €5.32 | €4.18 | −21% |
| Reported EPS | €3.01 | €1.82 | −40% |
| Free cash flow | €225m | €214m | −5% |
| Adjusted OCF | €419m | €391m | −7% |
| Cash conversion | 103% | 105% | Stable |
| Net debt | €1,251m | €1,495m | +19% (Resco) |
| Leverage | 2.3x | 2.9x | Above 2.0–2.5x target |
| Dividend | €1.80 | €1.80 | Flat |
| ROIC | 9.8% | 9.5% | Modest decline |

FY2024 was resilient in a weak market: adjusted EBITA flat at €407m despite −2% revenue, supported by M&A synergies (€77m adjusted EBITDA from 2023 deals) and working-capital release. FY2025 was harder in H1 but management self-help drove a strong H2; full-year adjusted EBITA of €373m landed within the revised €370–390m range set at H1 2025. Reported profit after tax fell to €94m (€86m attributable) from €154m, reflecting €98m of adjusting items (ERP/digital €44m, plant closures €27m, restructuring).

Balance sheet: net debt rose to €1,495m after the Resco acquisition (€363m cash outflow in investing activities). Liquidity remained adequate — €955m (€355m cash + €600m undrawn RCF) at year-end 2025 vs €1,376m at end-2024. Goodwill and intangibles totalled €943m; tangible book value is thin (Yahoo: €82m), which matters for asset-based investors.

FY2026 outlook (from 2025 results): adjusted EBITA +17% CC to ~€435m (~€400m reported after FX); leverage reducing to ~2.6x; cash conversion >90%; no large M&A cash-out expected.

**Interim results**

| Metric | H1 2025 (30 Jul 2025) | H1 2026 (31 Jul 2026) |
|--------|----------------------|----------------------|
| Revenue | €1,677m (−3%) | €1,595m (−5%; flat CC) |
| Adjusted EBITA | €141m (8.4%) | €165m (10.3%) |
| Adjusted EPS | €1.37 | €1.81 (+32%) |
| Net debt | €1,583m | €1,528m |
| Leverage | 3.1x (peak) | 2.9x |
| Cash conversion | 124% | 97% (inventory build) |

H1 2025 was the trough: industrial project deferrals (Glass −40%, non-ferrous −22%), pricing pressure, and Resco financing pushed leverage to 3.1x. Management cut FY2025 guidance to €370–390m. H1 2026 shows clear inflection — adjusted EBITA +42% CC — driven by steel (adjusted EBITA +69% CC to €126m) while industrial remained weak (revenue −13%). FY2026 adjusted EBITA guidance confirmed at €400m; net debt expected ~€1,400m and leverage ~2.6x by year-end.

**Trading updates**

Q3 2024 and Q1 2025 trading updates are indexed; the November 2025 update (four months to October 2025) reported adjusted EBITA of €136m at a 12.7% margin, confirming H2 2025 momentum and reiterating full-year €370–390m guidance (subsequently delivered at €373m).

**Trend assessment**

Revenue is structurally pressured by cyclical lows in steel and industrial capex, Chinese export competition, and EUR translation (USD/INR weakness). Earnings quality is improving faster than top line: margins recovered from H1 2025 trough to H2 2025 and H1 2026 on self-help, not demand. Cash generation remains a strength but H1 2026 saw temporary working-capital absorption (inventory intensity 31.0% vs 26.3% at FY2025) ahead of H2 order books.

**Gaps**

No SEC 20-F in the index (UK RNS regime only). Companies House filings are UK entity accounts, not consolidated group statements. Quarterly income in `financials_annual.json` is empty.
risks_and_flags:
**Cyclical and competitive.** Steel refractory demand tracks global steel production (WSA: ~−2% in 2025; soft H1 2026). Chinese steel and refractory exports depress pricing and volumes in India, META, Latin America, and East Asia. Industrial project activity (Glass, non-ferrous) remains ~40% below historic levels; >€50m of project revenue deferred past 2026 per H1 2026 filing. Recovery timing uncertain — management does not expect material demand uplift before H2 2026 at earliest for industrial projects.

**Leverage and liquidity.** Post-Resco leverage at 2.9x exceeds the through-cycle target of 1.0–2.0x (temporary up to ~2.5x for M&A). H1 2025 interim risk disclosure flagged constrained capital allocation from deteriorating leverage. Refinancing activity in H1 2026 (€350m term loan, €450m Schuldschein) addresses maturities but floating-rate exposure rose (69% floating). Reverse stress-testing in going-concern disclosures identifies EBITDA levels that could breach debt covenants; mitigants include cost cuts, working-capital reduction, capex cuts, covenant waiver, or dividend cancellation — not modelled in base case.

**Pension and legacy obligations.** Non-current defined benefit liabilities of €232m (FY2025 balance sheet). Ongoing pension charges in net finance expenses (~€11m FY2025). EU merger remedies include onerous contract present-value adjustments (Oberhausen provision).

**Operational and governance.** Fatal workplace incidents reported in 2024 and H1 2025; TRIF increased in H1 2026 (5.4 per million hours) as reporting scope expanded. ERP/digital transformation (~€100m programme) carries execution risk — H1 2026 North America ERP go-live caused invoicing backlogs. Digital transformation risk level increased in H1 2026 principal risk review.

**Regulatory and trade.** Tariff exposure (US-EU 15%, potential Brazil-US 50% on finished goods), EU steel quota changes, and Brazil refractory duty investigation — timing and impact uncertain (potential medium-term tailwind per November 2025 update). ESRS sustainability reporting burden cited by management as resource drain.

**Accounting.** Heavy reliance on adjusted metrics (€98m adjusting items in FY2025). Put-option revaluation for minority stakes in Jinan New Emei and Chongqing creates volatile non-operating items. Accounting policy restatements in 2025 (amortisation presentation) affect comparability.

**Going concern.** Both H1 2025 and H1 2026 interim statements confirm going-concern basis after downside scenario testing; covenant compliance reported in both periods.

RiskTags: cyclical, competitive, leverage, pension, regulatory, governance, other
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is moderate — dominated by results RNS and syndicated equity commentary rather than deep sell-side research.

Material items from `news_manifest.json`:

- **31 Jul 2026** — "RHI Magnesita Q2 Earnings Call Highlights" / "H1 2026 Earnings Call Highlights": H1 adjusted EBITA +42% CC; FY2026 €400m guidance maintained; self-help and steel strength offset FX and weak industrial projects.
- **30 Jul 2025** — TradingView: "RHIM: Margin and profit growth offset revenue decline; guidance and deleveraging on track" (around H1 2025 results).
- **10 Nov 2025** — Proactive Investors: "RHI Magnesita surges 15% after hailing effects of cost-cutting, plant closures" (aligned with November 2025 trading update showing H2 margin recovery).
- **2 Mar 2026** — Investors' Chronicle: "RHI Magnesita at the mercy of global trade" (tariff/trade exposure framing around FY2025 results).
- **17 Nov 2025** — "EU-backed RAPTOR sets new standard in refractory recycling" (sustainability/innovation).
- **28 Jan 2025** (RNS index) — Completion of Resco transaction (€391m; largest deal since 2017 merger).

Management changes: directorate changes noted in RNS index (Mar, Nov 2025; Nov 2025); IR contact shifted from Chris Bucknall to Alexander Ordosch by H1 2026. No CEO change — Stefan Borgas remains in post.

News coverage is adequate for event-driven updates but thin on independent fundamental analysis; several headlines reference RHI Magnesita India (NSE:RHIM), a separate listed entity.
research_rationale: Filing-backed evidence supports the screen’s value case — leader franchise, 5% yield, strong cash conversion, and a visible self-help earnings inflection — but elevated leverage, cyclical demand weakness, and industrial project deferrals prevent full confirmation of an unqualified Strong Buy.
